quote: if you want to accurately model AI lab financials, you need to understand their subscription limits.
claim: SemiAnalysis frames subscription limits as a financial-modelling input, not a buyer guide.

quote: The 5-hour limit resets many times within a week, so a month is capped by the weekly limits.
claim: Monthly API-equivalent value is capped by weekly limits, not 5-hour windows.

quote: Reading from the cache costs almost nothing on some plans and may not move the meter at all.
claim: Cache reads barely count against plan meters, driving large API-equivalent multiples.

quote: Researchers isolated each token type (input, cache write, cache read, output) with targeted prompts, recorded meter movement per request, added steps until error within +-5%, then priced tokens at API rates.
claim: Controlled measurement of token-type rates per plan, converted to API-equivalent value.

quote: Anthropic offers roughly 5x OpenAI's API-equivalent value at mid-tier models and about 4x for Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6.1 Sol; OpenAI halved the $200 plan's value and added a $500 tier; an A/B test gave one account ~20% lower limits.
claim: Published 2026-10-05; shows provider limits change silently and per model.

quote: Rates apply to Anthropic Pro and Max, OpenAI Plus ($20), Pro 100, Pro 200 and a $500 tier; Fable usage counts against only 50% of a $200 plan limit.
claim: Per-model meters mean value is model-specific, supporting exact-variant evidence rules.

quote: Parsed 14,973 local Claude Code session files, deduplicated by request ID like ccusage; 33.28B input tokens, 122M output, 96.4% cache hit, 2026-07-29 to 2026-08-28, one Max 20x seat at $200/month.
claim: User-reported single-seat measurement: Opus 5 equivalent $26,187/month vs $200 fee, break-even ~255M tokens.

quote: A rolling 5-hour cap plus an unpublished weekly cap means the multiple can change without a price change.
claim: Subscription multiples are unstable because weekly caps are unpublished.

quote: Input and output list prices get all the attention. At agent volume they barely matter.
claim: Cache-read share dominates API-equivalent cost for agentic use.

quote: Measured over 2026 10/05 – 10/12, a week of Claude Max 20x is worth about $1,751 of official API usage
claim: Max 20x ~ $1,751/week API-equivalent; Pro $170/week; Team Premium $863; ratio Max20x/Pro ~10x not 20x.

quote: Anthropic says Max 20x gives 20 times Pro's usage, but that multiple applies to the 5-hour window.
claim: Advertised multiplier applies to 5-hour window; weekly cap ratio is ~10x.

quote: Most tokens in a long session are cache reads, and cache reads barely count against a plan.
claim: Cache reads barely consume plan allowance.

quote: Data is remeasured every Monday after 04:00 UTC over the past 7 days; a plan is published only after at least 5 accounts; changes over 15% manually checked.
claim: Weekly cadence with account-count and anomaly gates; Max 5x still 1 account.

quote: Dollars are API-list equivalents, not cash charged on the subscription. Monthly is the weekly allowance ×4, a projection.
claim: Allowance expressed as API-list dollars with a x4 monthly projection.

quote: Claude Max 20x ($200): ~$2,155/week (range $2,136-$2,174); OpenAI Pro 20x ($200): ~$1,532/week; SuperGrok Heavy ($300): ~$400.5/week, snapshot 2026-09-25.
claim: Cross-vendor weekly allowance comparison; Claude figure differs from Wokey's $1,751 a week later.

quote: Four models across games, visual scenes, CAD, PCB, and simulated robotics, with per-round evidence and no aggregate score.
claim: RemakeBench publishes per-round evidence, no aggregate quality score, so plan capacity is not combined into a single value rank.

quote: Avg cost column shows some entries marked 'includes provider estimates' and lists providers such as Anthropic, OpenAI Codex and a Grok CLI subscription.
claim: Costs are API-equivalent estimates alongside quality results, a partial quality/cost link.

quote: Anthropic publishes no absolute message counts at any tier; OpenAI publishes them for Codex in fine per-model detail
claim: Provider-published limit transparency differs: Codex ranges published, Anthropic not.

quote: The usage limits for local messages and cloud tasks share a five-hour window. Additional weekly limits may apply.
claim: Codex limits share a five-hour window with additional weekly limits.

quote: Dated log: 30 Jul 2026 verification, 5 Sep GPT-6 Astra added, a temporary 50% Claude Code weekly increase expired 13 Sep and never appeared in docs.
claim: Provider-claim based, with change log of limit shifts.

quote: Anthropic’s ratios are all per five-hour session: Pro gives at least 5× Free, and Max gives 5× or 20× Pro.
claim: Vendor-stated ratios, no measurement.

quote: Your usage depends on how complex the prompt is, which features you use, and how long the chat runs.
claim: Page explicitly does not tie limits to quality; advises trying newer model at lower effort first.

quote: Last updated October 14, 2026; Grok X Subscription replaced SuperGrok plans on October 12; Grok uses one weekly pool shared with Cursor.
claim: Plan structures change frequently; note SuperGrok replaced.

quote: Lower bound: chat use in Claude and ChatGPT is not in local logs, so the real value can be higher.
claim: Value multiple is a floor because chat use is not logged.

quote: Amounts are API equivalents. On a subscription you do not pay them; they show the size of your use.
claim: Same framing as ValueRank's API-equivalent numerator but user-local.

quote: Window estimate: API-equivalent use up to the window's peak reading divided by peak percentage; median over windows reaching at least 10%; plans.json verified 2026-10-02.
claim: Allowance derived from vendor interface percentages plus local logs.

quote: At my current pace, would the API be cheaper than my subscription over the next 30 days?
claim: Tool projects API-equivalent cost over 30 days vs plan prices; no quality link.

quote: Limits are enforced on two simultaneous rolling windows: a 5-hour session window and a 7-day weekly window.
claim: Claude limits use 5-hour and 7-day windows.

quote: Some use rolling windows. Some use fixed resets. Some are transparent about their numbers. Most aren't.
claim: Opaque limits are the norm; guide uses estimates where unpublished, no benchmark ties.

quote: Claude Max multiplies Claude Pro's allowance: 5x for $100/mo or 20x for $200/mo, per rolling 5-hour session
claim: Max figures are the site's arithmetic from Pro baseline, not published counts.

quote: usage is measured in compute, so long conversations, big attachments, and heavier models drain it faster
claim: Allowance consumption depends on model and task; no benchmark link.

quote: A percentage means little until you know how much of the window has passed, so lpm judges every meter against the clock.
claim: Pace tracker, not a value ranking; prices tokens at list.

quote: tracks your Claude, OpenAI Codex, xAI Grok, Cursor, Devin, and Droid (Factory AI) usage limits in real time.

quote: The weekly limit and each per-model cap reset on their own rolling weekly schedule, not on a fixed calendar day.
